title.narrative: Realising the Rights of Older People through Inclusive Social Protection Systems, Accountability, and Resilience Strengthening (ROAR) Programme in Ethiopia, Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania

description.narrative:
Objective 1: Social protection mechanisms are able to meet the needs of older people across the four countries • Objective 1.1: Increase older people’s access to inclusive (age -and gender-inclusive) and adequate social protection systems/programmes. • Objective 1.2: Influence the design and strengthen the implementation of adaptive shock responsive social protection systems/programmes able meet the needs of older people.
Objective 2: A community movement for change is informed and empowered to advocate for the needs and rights of older people • Objective 2.1: Foster structures and platforms that ensure the active participation and influence of older people, communities, and CSOs in decision-making processes related to the rights, needs and challenges experienced by older people. • Objective 2.2: Decision making processes by community leadership, programme implementers, local and national authorities engage with and reflect the needs and priorities of older people.
Objective 3: Promote the creation of protective and inclusive environments that address the rights, needs and issues of older women and men.
Objective 4: Foster learning and collaboration by sharing programme impact, research findings and learnings with the HelpAge global network, partners and stakeholders to create adaptive and impactful programming for older people.
Older People, Women, People with disabilities

Realizing the Rights of Older People thought Inclusive Social Protection Systems, Accountability, and Resilience Strengthening (ROAR) is a multi-country program implemented across Ethiopia, Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania. The overarching goal of the program is to empower older people to lead dignified, secure, and resilient lives.

participating-org.narrative: Ministry of Labour, Gender and Social Action

description.narrative: Tete, Marara, Cahora Bassa, Changara and Chiuta Districts

activity-description.narrative: Forming and strengthening of OPAs; Supporting OCMGs and older women's training; Conduct leadership training for older women

sector.narrative: Prioritising Gender Equality The proposed interventions will specifically be tailored to prioritise gender equality, creating inclusive environments that address the needs and challenges faced by older women. Older women are often excluded by many stakeholders which focus on the equality of girls and women of reproductive age – however, HelpAge’s research has shown that compounding years of inequality and gender dynamics are more pronounced in older age, with older women suffering from higher levels of poverty and discrimination than older men. Building on recent research, the programme will advocate for gender responsive social protection programmes and initiatives, and support older women both participate as well as lead local community based organisations which are able to effectively demand for change.

Protection and People In advocating for the implementation of nationally owned inclusive social protection systems and programmes, our aim is to protect the rights of older people and increase their overall wellbeing – reducing poverty and hunger, and the inequalities faced by extremely vulnerable individuals and their communities.

Strengthening Governance Working with older people, local partners and other development actors, we will focus on strengthening social protection systems to be more inclusive as well as responsive and adaptive to shocks by: 1) Working with governments to influence the design and implementation of inclusive, age-and gender- responsive social protection systems which can meet the needs of older women and men 2) Fostering the active participation, voice and influence of older people, their communities and civil society organisations in decision-making processes - calling for accountable institutions that uphold the rights of older people 3) Creating communities of practice at local and national levels and across the HelpAge network to promote civil society action - sharing evidence and learning, helping to build stronger more engaged bodies
